essence: Dated and signed, it turns outward: the compassionate Lord pacifies the world's heat instantly.
What began in the heart ends in the world: private recognition cools the world.
The colophon dates the composition (Pauṣa, Kṛṣṇa Daśamī) and signs it (Abhinavagupta), then turns to the world.

sections.SUMMARY: Dated and signed, it turns outward: the compassionate Lord pacifies the world's heat instantly — what began in the heart ends in the world.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes the colophon and pacification: dated composition, signed author, then outward turn — private recognition cools the world.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **pauṣa** — month of Pauṣa: the date.
* **kṛṣṇadaśamī** — dark tenth: the lunar day.
* **abhinavagupta** — Abhinavagupta: the author, signing.
* **stava** — hymn: the composition named.
* **yena** — by whom: devotee or hymn, undivided in effect.
* **vibhu** — pervasive Lord: the one who pacifies.
* **bhavamarusantāpa** — desert-heat of becoming: the world's suffering.
* **śamayati** — pacifies: the Lord's act.
* **jhaṭiti** — instantly: the speed.
* **dayālu** — compassionate: the Lord's quality.
sections.EXPLANATION: In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn: dated, signed. By whom (yena) — devotee or hymn, undivided in effect — the pervasive (vibhuḥ), compassionate (dayāluḥ) Lord becomes (bhavati), pacifies (śamayati) the world's desert-heat of becoming — instantly (jhaṭiti). The dated hymn turns outward: private recognition cools the world. It moves from colophon (date, author, work) to pacification (the Lord's act) to speed (instantly) — beginning in inward dissolution (v.1), ending in world-pacification.
sections.BOUNDARY: Whether 'yena' refers to devotee or hymn is unresolved. Whether 'bhavamarusantāpa' is physical or existential heat is unresolved.
sections.RELATED:
* Bhairavastava v.1 — veneration of the all-pervading Lord.
* Bhairavastava v.9 — rejoicing consciousness, obtaining as vision.
* Tantrāloka — the Absolute's compassion (dayā).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as pacification of the world
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of pacification (śamana); the vyabhicāri is compassion (karuṇā) of the dated hymn. The rasa is the tranquility of compassion — the hymn that began in inward dissolution ends in world-pacification.
